about: Research for gov-congress-passes-policy-laws (plan unit C2, docs/reports/world-governing-plan-2026-10-29.md): for each federal-level question, the law in force, the latest Senate floor vote on it, what in the town reads it, and whether a Congress drawn from real party shares can honestly clear 60 Senate votes on it. Nothing reads this file yet; unit C3 wires the chosen questions. The ranked candidates are in docs/research/evidence/federal-questions-2026-10-29.md.
method: Three finders researched nine questions each from fetched pages, and a separate verifier refetched every roll call, statute quote and code line; its corrections are applied here. The writer then refetched every roll call cited: Senate votes from Voteview's roll-call API (senate.gov refused fetches with 403) and House votes from the Clerk's XML. Code lines were read on main at the commit this file was added on.

fields.question: The question key.
fields.currentLaw: The law in force, quoted word for word from the page at currentLawUrl, with any gap between it and the game's starting law.
fields.latestFloorVote: The latest Senate floor vote that set or answers the question's law, since 60 votes are a Senate test; the latest House vote where the Senate never voted; null where neither chamber voted. yeas and nays count members only; parties gives [yeas, nays] by party (R, D, I); a Vice President's tie-break is in tieBreak. verified is true where the verifier confirmed the counts and the writer refetched them.
fields.otherVotes: The other chamber's vote, the votes that show or deny 60 Senate votes, and committee votes where no floor vote exists, in the same shape.
fields.reader: file:line where an engine reads this question's law today, or null.
fields.readerReads: What that reader reads: key (the question itself), series (the law series the question would change; the key itself is read nowhere), budget-line (a federal budget line), or outcome-web (a lagged or price-level read that writes no lawApplied row).
fields.reachesNamedResident: Whether a law on this question would, through that reader today, leave a lawApplied row on a named town resident that reachedBy lists: the C3 done-when's test.
fields.cheapestReader: The cheapest change that would give the question a real reader in the town, or 'Already built'.
fields.sixtyVotes: Whether the move Congress would make on this question has a floor record of 60 Senate votes that today's party shares would repeat.
fields.why: The reason for sixtyVotes, from the votes above.

questions.question: us-policy-positions:health-human-services.medicaid-work-requirement

questions.question: us-tax-terms:federal.excise-tax-terms
questions.currentLaw: 26 U.S.C. 4081(a)(2)(A): "in the case of gasoline other than aviation gasoline, 18.3 cents per gallon"; "in the case of diesel fuel or kerosene, 24.3 cents per gallon". The 0.1-cent leaking-underground-storage-tank rate under (a)(2)(B) makes the gasoline rate charged 18.4 cents, the figure the repo's own fuel research uses (household-prices-2026.json, "federal 18.4"). Under (d)(1) the rates "shall be 4.3 cents per gallon after September 30, 2028" (P.L. 117-58 div. H sec. 80102 moved that date from Sept 30, 2022), and the 0.1-cent rate also ends then (d)(3). The aviation ticket tax ends under sec. 4261(k)(1)(A)(ii), "ending on September 30, 2028" (P.L. 118-63 sec. 1302(b)(1)). P.L. 119-21 "establishes a 1% excise tax on certain electronic transfers of funds from the United States to a foreign country" from Jan 1, 2026 (Wikipedia, One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

One catch for the C3 test: the price engine records a price law's reach on the household (src/core2/modules/place-prices.ts:1321, recordApplied :763-796), and reachedBy keeps only person ids (src/core2/law-reach/host.ts:350), so the rule must record the paying person or reachedBy must read households. It needs a US starting row of 18.4 cents a gallon of gasoline that lapses to 4.3 cents after Sept 30, 2028. The prefix us-tax-terms: is not FEDERAL_QUESTION_PREFIX (src/core2/modules/laws.ts:236), so C1's question list must include it.
questions.why: Extending expiring federal excise terms cleared 60 twice in five years: 69-30 with 19 Republicans (2021) and 88-4 (2024), each inside a larger authorization bill. Raising a rate has no bipartisan vote; the new remittance excise passed by reconciliation. The law supplies a dated cause with no dice: the fuel rates fall to 4.3 cents after Sept 30, 2028. Because the key is generic, C3 must define yes as extending the expiring sec. 4081 rates, and because an extension keeps a price unchanged, the proof must compare the town's fuel charge by record id against a twin where the rate lapsed. A played year opened on 2026-10-12 ends about 11.5 months before the lapse; the 2021 extension passed the Senate about 13 months before its lapse, so a stance that reads time-to-lapse can bring the bill up inside a year only near its end.

questions.question: us-federal-positions:monetary-financial.cap-consumer-loan-interest
questions.currentLaw: No general federal ceiling. Military Lending Act, 10 U.S.C. 987(b): a creditor "may not impose an annual percentage rate of interest greater than 36 percent" "with respect to the consumer credit extended to a covered member or a dependent of a covered member" (Pub. L. 109-364 sec. 670(a)). Federal credit unions, 12 U.S.C. 1757(5)(A)(vi): "the rate of interest may not exceed 15 per centum per annum on the unpaid balance inclusive of all finance charges, except that the Board may establish—" a higher temporary ceiling. The game has no US starting row for this key.

questions.question: us-federal-positions:emergencies.states-share-disaster-costs

otherVotes.motion: To order the bill reported (CRS R48856: "voted 57 to 3 to order the bill reported")
otherVotes.what: A committee vote, not a floor vote; "Companion legislation has not currently been introduced in the Senate." The CRS report does not describe a change to the 75 percent share.

questions.readerNote: Nothing reads the key. declare() (src/core2/modules/disasters.ts:237-269) pays FEMA Public Assistance's recorded federal obligation from the Treasury to the county's and town's governments on the declaration date (:268-269). Its payHouseholds (:307-336) pays housing assistance into the counted residents' account, which is not the sec. 5172 or 5170b share.
questions.cheapestReader: Scale declare()'s payment by the federal share in force over 75 percent. It reaches government books, not a named person, and only in a year with a recorded declaration (src/core2/data/disasters/declarations.json, latest 2026-10-09).
questions.why: Nothing that shifts disaster costs to states has reached either floor, and the one reform bill has only a committee vote and no Senate companion.

questions.question: us-federal-positions:science-communications.national-data-privacy
questions.currentLaw: No comprehensive federal statute, only sector laws, for example COPPA, 15 U.S.C. 6502(a)(1): "It is unlawful for an operator of a website or online service directed to children, or any operator that has actual knowledge that it is collecting personal information from a child, to collect personal information from a child in a manner that ...". Biometric Update (Dec 23, 2025): "For more than a decade, Congress has promised a national privacy statute and repeatedly fallen short".

otherVotes.bill: H.R. 8152 (117th), American Data Privacy and Protection Act
otherVotes.motion: To report the bill ("voted to pass H.R. 8152, the American Data Privacy and Protection Act (ADPPA) by a vote of 53-2")
otherVotes.what: A committee vote with no party breakdown on the page. The 2024 successor's markup was canceled (CyberScoop, June 27, 2024: "A House panel abruptly canceled its plans Thursday to take action on a sweeping federal privacy bill" ...).

questions.readerNote: The business duty reads only the state key: DATA_PRIVACY_QUESTION (src/core2/modules/business.ts:1269-1270), BUSINESS_DUTIES (:1283-1296) and readBusinessDuty's lawInForce (:1319), adding the cost only for a governing yes (:1342-1343). The state key's reach row is records-only (reach-group-a.json:601-617).
questions.cheapestReader: One more BUSINESS_DUTIES entry with the federal key and businessDataPrivacyShareOfCosts: each employing town business pays a monthly compliance cost, recorded as the law applied through lawOfCost (business.ts:1371-1394). It reaches named organizations, and a person only through their books.
questions.why: No comprehensive privacy bill has reached either floor: the 53-2 committee vote in 2022 stalled and the 2024 markup was canceled. There is no floor record to set a consensus share and no evidence of 60.

questions.question: us-tax-terms:federal.sales-tax-terms
questions.currentLaw: No federal sales tax. The pending H.R. 25 (119th) is titled "To promote freedom, fairness, and economic opportunity by repealing the income tax and other taxes, abolishing the Internal Revenue Service, and enacting a national sales tax to be administered primarily by the States." It was introduced on January 3, 2025 and "referred to the Committee on Ways and Means". src/core2/data/legislature/series-powers.json:12-14 gives sales-tax the state and local levels only ("No federal sales tax").
questions.readerNote: syncSalesTax (src/core2/modules/budgets.ts:848-880) reads lawInForce(api, 'sales-tax') at :852 and skips the federal level at :865. The key itself is read nowhere.
questions.cheapestReader: Drop that skip and pay the Treasury's share in syncSalesTax, but there is no federal law to read.
questions.why: No federal sales tax exists, and the one bill to create one has had no committee or floor vote.

questions.question: us-tax-terms:federal.corporate-tax-terms
questions.currentLaw: 26 U.S.C. 11(b): "The amount of the tax imposed by subsection (a) shall be 21 percent of taxable income." P.L. 119-21 changed the terms, not the rate: "SEC. 70301. FULL EXPENSING FOR CERTAIN BUSINESS PROPERTY. (a) Made Permanent." and "SEC. 70302. FULL EXPENSING OF DOMESTIC RESEARCH AND EXPERIMENTAL EXPENDITURES".

questions.readerNote: payProfitTaxes (employer-taxes.ts:179-345) reads lawInForce(api, 'corporate-income-tax'), including the federal row at 21 (src/core2/data/laws/starting-law.json:65-73), on each organization-owned business's quarterly profit, and records the law as applied to that organization. bill-catalog.json:312-319 already lets the federal level raise or lower law:corporate-income-tax (the player's menu). The outcome-web 'state-corporate-rate' readers (src/core2/modules/outcome-web.ts:287-293 and :306) read the state level only. The key itself is read nowhere.
questions.cheapestReader: Point the question at the existing series, or drop the duplicate key. It reaches named organizations, not a named resident.
questions.why: Corporate tax terms moved only by party-line reconciliation (2017 at 51-48; 2022 and 2025 at 50-50 with the Vice President). The one bipartisan attempt failed Senate cloture 48-44 with three Republicans.

planCorrections: The plan's C2 row says the minimum wage "failed cloture 42-58 in 2021": it was a motion to waive the Budget Act (60 needed), not cloture (Voteview RS1170074).

The plan's C2 row says the stock-trading ban never reached the floor: it passed the House 232-198 on July 22, 2026 and failed Senate cloture 53-47 on Sept 30, 2026. Data privacy indeed never reached a floor.
The verifier's party split for H.R. 815 record vote 154 (April 23, 2024) gave Democrats 47-2; Voteview's roll call reads 46-2, which sums to the 79 yeas.

The federal yes on the Medicaid work requirement never reaches the town's chain (src/core2/modules/laws.ts:191-207 writes a US answer for a state-level question only where the state gives none), and that writer ignores the research's operativeAt (2027-01-01).

us-federal-positions:health.medicare-drug-price-negotiation has no US starting row, so the engine treats a law in force since 2022 as absent; C1 needs a US yes row (42 U.S.C. 1320f) before the key is admitted.

The us-tax-terms: prefix is not FEDERAL_QUESTION_PREFIX (src/core2/modules/laws.ts:236); a US-only starting row lands at the federal level only because no state answers it, and C1's question-list filter must include the prefix.

The world's Congress files only policy-question provisions on PLATFORM_QUESTIONS (src/core2/modules/world-legislating.ts:469-498), never a law-amount provision, so a law series (payroll tax, income tax) cannot be filed by Congress today.
